item.title: Verbose beta 234
item.description:
Ask your library, Apple Watch capture, and a Native look that follows Apple

Mac

  • Ask your library a question and get an answer that cites each recording and time. Verbose finds the matching passages on your device, Apple Intelligence answers from those alone, and Copy puts the answer and its sources on the clipboard.
  • Choose where Ask looks: All, This week, Thoughts, Meetings, or a project. If nothing there matches, Verbose says so instead of guessing, and without Apple Intelligence you get the matching passages and the reason.
  • Save a question as a recipe to ask it again on demand or every week. Recipes sync between your Mac and iPhone, schedules stay on each device, and each scheduled run sends a notification with the first line of the answer.
  • Ask's index stays on your device, and nothing from your transcripts leaves it. It updates in the background, never while you record or transcribe, forgets a recording you delete, and Delete all data removes it with your questions and recipes.
  • What's new sorts each build's changes by platform, with yours first. Changes for your other devices fold under Also on, and a line with more to say opens when you tap or click it.
  • Press ⌘K to search or ask from one field, and click a citation to play that moment. Search or ask also sits at the top of the sidebar, right-click a citation to open its transcript, and in the Native look the toolbar's search field asks on Return.
  • Right-click Record, or choose File › Record As, to pick one of six ways to record. Each choice has its Verbose icon, and File › Record As › Meeting replaces the separate Record Meeting item.
  • The Native look follows macOS 27 and uses your Mac's accent color for what you click. Red marks only recording, the warm background, glow, gradient cards, and shadows are gone, and widgets are black, like Apple Music's.
  • In the Native look, Record is a toolbar button, and the floating record button is gone. Click it for a voice note, or click its arrow for Dictate, Live captions, Import, and the six ways to record.
  • In the Native look, the Library opens as a table you can sort by any column. Switch to List in the toolbar to see what was said in each recording.
  • In the Native look, Home, transcripts, and Settings follow Apple's own layouts. Home uses grouped sections, a transcript reads in a centered column over a glass player bar, and Settings shows each pane with a colored icon.
  • Moments adds a Marked filter for the moments you mark while recording. Every filter shows its count, and where a mark came from reads the same in Moments and on the transcript, such as Mac · ⌃⌥B.
  • Smaller fixes. Pills, chips, and switches match across Verbose style, By day folds silent thoughts into one row, transcript playback is sage, and the app audio picker opens System Settings.

Also on iPhone and Apple Watch

iPhone

  • Touch and hold Record to pick one of six ways to record, or tap it for a voice note.
  • The Native look follows Apple's apps, with the system accent and red only for recording.
  • In the Native look, Record sits in the tab bar and opens a recorder like Voice Memos'.
  • In the Native look, Home, the Library, and transcripts follow Apple's own apps.
  • The Library opens with one row of tiles, so your recordings start higher up.
  • The Verbose style recorder puts Mark moment, Stop & transcribe, and Pause by your thumb.
  • Screens, tabs, and rows appear at once, without rising or sliding in.
  • Smaller fixes.

Apple Watch

  • Record a voice note or a thought from your wrist, and your iPhone transcribes it.
  • Tap Mark, or double-tap your fingers on a watch that supports it, to mark a moment.
  • Recording keeps going when you lower your wrist or your iPhone is out of reach.
  • Add Record and Today's thoughts to your watch face.
